newsitem.title: USA: AWAY ON BUSINESS: The hotel crunch.
newsitem.headline: AWAY ON BUSINESS: The hotel crunch.

text.p: The well-documented crunch in hotel space that has shut some business travelers out of their favourite inns shows no sign of easing.

The latest travel forecast from the Travel Industry Association of America shows a robust travel situation this spring in both the leisure and business sectors. But persistence and timing can often land a room even in the busiest cities.
One path is to use a consolidator -- operators who buy up blocks of hotel space at favourable rates and re-sell them.
One such company, Hotel Reservations Network, has just opened up a new Web site -- www.180096hotel.com -- on which travelers can shop for hotel space in 14 major U.S. and European cities.
After picking a city, the traveller enters a date or dates, number of nights and how many people in the party and smoking or no-smoking preferences.
The company's computer files are then scanned and the site displays the hotels that have space, along with the price. A further click provides details about the property itself.
David Litman, of Hotel Reservations Network, said the new arrangement was an improvement over a previous site it operated and that it was being called up 3.6 million times a month.

If the customer finds a room he or she wants, it can be booked right then and there. Litman said confirmation currently comes back by telephone, fax or e-mail, but in a few months there will be instantaneous confirmation while the customer is signed on to the site.

A recent check of the site found symptoms of the hotel crunch problem -- one that has been caused by increased levels of travel at a time when the hotel industry has not greatly expanded the number of available rooms.
The site showed no room available in New Orleans from the Hotel Reservations Network inventory on a mid-April date.

At the same time, a check of space in Chicago for a date in early May that coincides with an annual supermarket industry convention that soaks up most hotel space found several rooms, ranging in price from $85 to $279 a night.
Travelers can also check on rooms and make reservations by phone -- at 1-800-964-6835.
A report in the April issue of Travel & Leisure Magazine has some other tips on finding a room when the "no vacancy" sign seems to be everywhere.
One is simply to keep trying, since cancellations come in all the time. Another is to learn what time of the day a hotel releases reservations that have not been claimed and are not guaranteed.

That usually happens between 4 p.m. and 6 p.m., though the magazine warns that this approach has its perils since a growing number of hotels demand a guarantee, and there may not be that many rooms opened up at the last minute.

The report also recommends travelers check into hotel room hot lines operated by some cities, check out suburban or airport locations with easy access to public transit and try to build up a relationship with the hotel management so they will be regarded as loyal and favoured customers.

Business travelers: Question, complaint or pet peeve? Send them to Away on Business, c/o Reuters, Room 1170, 311 S. Wacker Dr., Chicago 60606.
